name: DeepSeek LLM 7B
description:
Here is how to read the DeepSeek LLM 7B config.json. The architecture class is LlamaForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 4,096: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 102,400 × 4,096: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 32, so each head sees 128 dimensions (4,096 / 32). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 4096 / 32 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 32, so this is multi-head attention (MHA): every query head keeps its own key/value.

num_hidden_layers is 30: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 11,008. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 4,096-wide stream is projected up, activated with silu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 4,096 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is. rope_theta is 10000.0: that is the wavelength of the rotary embedding. A larger theta keeps distant tokens from aliasing after a full rotation.

vocab_size is 102,400. 102,400 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is false, so the input embedding matrix and the output LM head are separate learned matrices rather than a shared transpose.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/deepseek-llm-7b-base/blob/main/config.json.
